After the Decision to Halt Manual Car Washes in Saudi Arabia: Your Complete Guide to Making the Switch

If you own a manual car wash in Saudi Arabia, you're no doubt keeping an eye on how quickly the car wash industry is changing. With rising labor costs, tighter water-conservation requirements, and stricter regulations, running a manual car wash has become harder than ever.

At the same time, the market is shifting toward more efficient solutions such as automatic and mechanized car wash systems, which offer higher throughput, lower water consumption, and a more consistent customer experience. WashThru provides end-to-end solutions to help car wash owners make the switch from manual to automatic — covering site assessment, equipment selection, installation, operation, and ongoing technical support.

In this guide, you'll learn why this shift is happening, the key differences between manual and automatic car washes, and how to choose the right system for your business to achieve the highest possible operational efficiency and return on investment.

The Ministry of Municipal, Rural Affairs and Housing has issued directives requiring car washes to meet strict standards, including:

  • Halting new permits for manual car washes in many regions of the Kingdom.
  • Requiring existing car washes to install water treatment and recycling systems.
  • Raising environmental compliance standards in coordination with the National Center for Environmental Compliance.
  • Encouraging digital and automated transformation in line with the economic goals of Vision 2030.

Why Did the Kingdom Make This Decision?

A single manual car wash uses between 150 and 300 liters of water per car, with no treatment or recycling systems in place. With thousands of car washes across the country, this places a massive strain on water resources in a nation that ranks among the most water-scarce in the world. That's why the government's direction is a deliberate, calculated move — not just an administrative decision made in passing.

What this means in practice: if your manual car wash is still operating, expect increasingly strict requirements when renewing its license. And if you're planning to open a new car wash, a manual car wash permit won't be an option in most regions.

Why the Drawbacks of Manual Car Washes Make Switching to Automatic Systems a Necessity

Even without the government decision, manual car washes suffer from structural issues that make them a fragile operating model in today's business environment.

1. High Water Consumption and Difficulty Controlling Waste

Water consumption is one of the biggest challenges facing manual car washes, since the amount of water used depends on each worker's technique and experience. This leads to significant variation in consumption and higher waste rates, especially during busy periods with heavy customer traffic.

2. Heavy Reliance on Operational Labor

The success of a manual car wash depends almost entirely on the availability and stability of its workforce. With rising recruitment costs and growing staff-management challenges, maintaining operational efficiency becomes harder compared to automated systems.

3. Inconsistent Service Quality From One Wash to the Next

It's difficult to maintain a consistent level of quality when workers' skills and experience vary. A customer might get an excellent experience on one visit, then a lower level of quality on the next — which affects customer satisfaction and loyalty.

4. Limited Capacity Relative to Demand

A manual car wash's operating capacity is tied to the number of workers and how fast they work, so its output remains inherently limited. In most cases, an average manual car wash doesn't exceed 40 to 60 cars a day, even during peak operating hours.

5. Growing Challenges in Regulatory Compliance

Environmental and regulatory requirements keep evolving, particularly around water conservation and waste treatment. With every new update, compliance requirements increase, adding operational and administrative burdens for manual car wash owners.

6. Higher Operating Costs Over the Long Run

While the initial setup cost may look lower, ongoing expenses such as salaries, water consumption, and daily maintenance drive up the project's total cost over time and eat into profit margins compared to modern automatic solutions.

The Smart Alternative: Automatic (Mechanized) Car Wash

An automatic car wash isn't just an alternative — it's a complete shift in the business model. Picture a car wash running with one or two workers instead of ten, washing three times as many cars per day, and using far less water, with the option to recycle it.

Quick Comparison: Manual vs. Automatic

  • Cars per day: 40–60 at a manual car wash, versus 100–300+ at an automatic car wash.
  • Workers needed: a manual car wash typically needs 6–12 workers, while an automatic car wash can run with just 1–3 people.
  • Water use per car: manual car washes use 150–300 liters, while automatic car washes use only about 50–80 liters, with the option to recycle water.
  • Wash quality: manual wash quality depends on the worker's experience and performance, while automatic car washes deliver uniform, consistent results every time.
  • Environmental compliance: manual car washes face bigger challenges meeting environmental requirements, while many automatic car washes come with built-in water treatment and recycling systems.
  • Operating costs: operating costs are higher at manual car washes due to heavy reliance on labor and water use, while automatic systems help lower operating expenses over the long run.
  • Scalability and growth: manual operations are constrained by labor and capacity, while automatic car washes make it possible to scale up and serve more customers without a major increase in costs.
  • The future of licensing and sustainability: modern regulations are moving toward more water- and resource-efficient solutions, making automatic car washes far better aligned with future requirements.

Three Types of Automatic Car Washes From WashThru: Which One Fits Your Project?

WashThru is a brand specialized in manufacturing and supplying automatic car wash systems, offering three different systems to suit various project sizes and site conditions.

System One: Automatic Rollover Car Wash

The rollover car wash is best suited to small or medium-sized locations. The equipment moves around the stationary car to clean it thoroughly, with high precision, in a short amount of time. WashThru offers three models:

  • RS-V4 model — balanced performance, suitable for most commercial locations
  • RH-V1 model — high efficiency with flexible operation
  • RA-V1 model — an all-in-one solution for heavy-duty use

Ideal for: fuel stations, small commercial centers, and independent car washes with limited space.

System Two: Automatic Tunnel Car Wash

The automatic tunnel car wash is the ideal solution for large-scale projects targeting a high volume of cars each day. The car moves through the tunnel on an automatic conveyor while being washed through a series of precise, consecutive stages.

Ideal for: large car wash businesses, car rental companies, car dealerships, and large commercial complexes. A tunnel system can serve more than 200 cars a day with no more than three staff members.

System Three: Automatic Touchless (Brushless) Car Wash

A touchless car wash relies on high-pressure water and specialized chemicals to clean the car without any physical contact, completely eliminating the risk of scratching.

Available models:

  • RF-V1 model — for medium commercial use
  • RCV-V1 model — an advanced solution for luxury and sensitive vehicles

Ideal for: luxury car owners, dealership centers, and premium car washes.

That's why WashThru offers several flexible solutions to help investors and car wash owners transition to automatic operation in a way that fits their resources and goals.

This option lets you spread the cost over manageable payments while starting operations and generating revenue during the repayment period.

2. Direct Cash Purchase

A direct cash purchase is the best option for investors seeking the highest long-term return on investment. By owning the equipment outright from day one, you can capture the full profit with no financing obligations or future installments, along with complete freedom to manage and grow the business.

3. Operating Lease

An operating lease lets you run an automatic car wash without a large capital investment. The client pays an operating fee or monthly rent to use the equipment, which reduces investment risk and makes this option a good fit for those looking to test the market or start the business at the lowest possible cost.

Frequently Asked Questions About Switching to Automatic Car Washes

If you're considering switching your manual car wash to an automatic one, here are the most common questions investors and car wash owners ask before making the decision.

1. Does an automatic car wash need a lot of space?

Not necessarily. Space requirements vary depending on the type of equipment and model chosen, and some devices are designed to work efficiently in limited spaces. For example, some rollover models can operate in spaces as small as roughly 6×6 meters, and the WashThru team will assess your site and recommend the best solution based on the available space.

2. How long does installation and setup take?

Installation and setup typically take between one and two weeks, depending on how ready the site is and the construction work required. This period covers installing and testing the equipment, confirming it's ready to operate, and training staff on operation and basic maintenance.

3. What happens if the equipment breaks down?

WashThru equipment relies on the Wash Cloud system, which continuously monitors equipment status. When an issue is detected, a maintenance ticket is automatically created and sent to the technical support team, helping speed up the response and reduce downtime.

4. Can an existing manual car wash site be converted into an automatic one?

Yes — this is one of the most common projects WashThru carries out. The process starts with assessing the current site and evaluating the infrastructure and available space, then preparing a complete conversion plan that makes the most of existing facilities and eases the transition to automatic operation as efficiently as possible.
